core.title: Give every DESIRED OUTCOME entry an id, a statement and its proving artifacts
core.given: A product capability decomposition containing What-Must-Be-True (DESIRED OUTCOME) entries that you are authoring, editing, inspecting or validating.
core.when: You add, edit, review or validate any DESIRED OUTCOME entry.
core.then: Every DESIRED OUTCOME entry declares its id, its statement, and the proving artifacts (the acceptances/tests that prove the statement).
prefer: Write the id, the statement and the list of proving acceptances/tests together when the entry is created.
When reviewing existing entries, flag or complete any entry lacking id, statement or proving artifacts.
avoid: A DESIRED OUTCOME entry missing its id, its statement, or its proving artifacts.
Listing proving artifacts that do not actually prove the entry's statement.
core.why: Downstream planning (per-WMBT acceptance coverage, feature grouping, smoke acceptances) operates over enumerated, well-shaped DESIRED OUTCOMES; an entry without id, statement or proof cannot be referenced or verified.
evidence: Each DESIRED OUTCOME entry in the product capability decomposition has a non-empty id, a non-empty statement and at least one referenced proving artifact (acceptance/test).
verification: Severity 2, disposition documentation-only: verified by reading the product capability decomposition; this rule preserves no automated detector.
Check vocabulary: a desired_outcome_entry is a What-Must-Be-True entry in a product capability decomposition; proving_artifacts are the acceptances/tests that prove the DESIRED OUTCOME statement.

Scope: the check establishes presence — a non-empty id, a non-empty statement and at least one referenced proving artifact per entry; whether a referenced artifact genuinely proves the statement is a review judgment covered by the avoid guidance, not a separate mechanical check.

fires: The planner adds a new DESIRED OUTCOME entry to a product capability decomposition.
The planner edits any field of an existing DESIRED OUTCOME entry.
The planner inspects, reviews or validates existing DESIRED OUTCOME entries in a product capability decomposition, even without editing them.
The planner restructures or regenerates a product capability decomposition that contains DESIRED OUTCOME entries.
doesNotFire: Work that neither authors, inspects nor validates DESIRED OUTCOME entries (e.g. editing unrelated planning documents).
Implementing code or tests for an already-shaped DESIRED OUTCOME (coder work, not planning).

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete artifact kinds that play the plan_artifact role and hold a product capability decomposition or DESIRED OUTCOME entries, so the file_kind activation fact can be evaluated in a given stack.

bunOnly.text: parity.implementation_preserved=false — a reference to the frozen ATDD-Bun sidecar's parity bookkeeping field.
bunOnly.reason: The sidecar's parity flags are bookkeeping of the Bun realization; the neutral core keeps only the rule-level severity, the documentation-only disposition and the absence of an automated detector.

neutralityNotes: The convention is method-level (DESIRED OUTCOME entries inside a product capability decomposition) and needed almost no neutralization; DESIRED OUTCOME and product capability are ATDD-method artifact names — also artifact params in the closed urn vocabulary — so they remain in the core. The only realization-specific content is the sidecar parity reference in verifier_detail[1]. Which concrete file kinds hold product capability decompositions / DESIRED OUTCOME entries is per-stack and is supplied through roles.plan_artifact.kinds; the id's concrete shape is left to each realization because bun.json states no value for it.
